lesson_title: Two Friends, One Till: the Partnership Year, Revised
hook_text: Every partnership quarrel is one of two sentences. Accounting answers both.
clip_script: Two friends open a shop. One brings more money. The other puts in longer hours. Within weeks, the dangerous sentences arrive: 'I invested more, so more belongs to me.' 'I work harder, so more belongs to me.' Every partnership quarrel ever recorded is one of those two — and the partnership agreement answers both before voices rise: a salary for the hours worked, interest for the money that waits, a ratio for whatever is left. Watch it run. The year's pot: three hundred thousand rand. Scoop one — pay for the hours: one-oh-eight and eighty-four. Scoop two — thanks to the waiting money: twenty-four and sixteen. Scoop three — the promised bonus: eight. What remains? Sixty thousand — shared three to two, thirty-six and twenty-four. Count the bowls: one sixty-eight plus one thirty-two — exactly three hundred thousand. The pot empties to the rand, and that emptiness is the proof: appropriation never makes or loses a cent. It only shares — fairly, on paper, with the friendship intact.
visual_style: Two friends at a single till; a glowing profit pot emptied by four labelled scoops into two bowls; the bowls balancing exactly against the pot on a scale; a signed agreement page glowing beneath it all.
mood: Warm but exact — fairness as arithmetic.
pacing: Conflict setup, four scoop beats, the empty-pot proof landing last.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and share the pot yourself.
